title: Model Rollback Protocol: When and How to Roll Back Production Models
content:
## When to Roll Back
Rollback is appropriate when ALL of the following apply:
1. Drift score exceeds critical threshold (PSI > 0.35, ADWIN > 0.30)
2. Model accuracy has dropped more than 5% from baseline
3. Retrain is not available within the next 2 hours
4. Business impact is confirmed (e.g., prediction volume indicates active serving)

## Rollback Decision Tree
```
Drift detected?
  ├─ Accuracy stable → Monitor, no rollback needed
  └─ Accuracy degraded
       ├─ Previous version available?
       │    ├─ Yes → Assess previous version drift score
       │    │         ├─ Previous version also drifted → No rollback (retrain only)
       │    │         └─ Previous version stable → ROLLBACK
       │    └─ No → Emergency retrain required
       └─ Only one version exists → Emergency retrain
```

## Rollback Execution Steps
1. Confirm target version: `GET /api/models/{model_id}/versions`
2. Shadow-deploy previous version alongside current version for 5 minutes
3. Validate accuracy parity on recent labeled samples
4. Switch traffic routing: 100% to previous version
5. Disable current version
6. Open retrain ticket immediately

## Post-Rollback Monitoring
- Monitor ADWIN score on rolled-back version for next 60 minutes
- If rolled-back version also drifts: root cause is data pipeline, not model
- Alert ML platform team and initiate root cause analysis

## Rollback SLA
- Detection → Decision: ≤ 15 minutes
- Decision → Execution: ≤ 10 minutes
- Total TTR (Time to Rollback): ≤ 25 minutes
